# Intake brief — evaluate-tune-progress watchdog test races on src/data tune journal

## Headline

Point the `evaluate-tune-progress` real-CLI test at a per-test temp data
root so its watchdog assertions never read the shared `src/data` directory,
removing the last concurrent-run race window.

## Problem statement

The `--watchdog` case in `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` asserts on
state in the **real** `src/data` directory (the journal scan and the CSV
digest), so a sibling vitest worker that momentarily holds a journal there —
or edits the tracked CSV — can fail it spuriously. The observed flake
(`expected ['enemy-configs.csv.tune-journal'] to deeply equal []`) was
already mitigated once by scoping the journal assertion to the run's own pid
(commit `88e6827a`, AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS), but the test still reads the shared
directory, so AC1 of it ("the test no longer reads shared mutable state in
`src/data`") is not yet satisfied in letter and two narrow race windows
remain: an unparseable foreign journal counts as owned, and a sibling suite
doing a real-edit `--tune` spawn could transiently change the CSV between the
test's two digest reads.

## Users

As a **developer running the unit suite in parallel**, I want the
`evaluate-tune-progress` watchdog test to observe only its own run, so a
concurrent worker's transient journal (or edit) can never fail my build.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The CLI's `--tune` data root is overridable per run (a seam in
   `resolveTuneCsvPath()` in `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — e.g. an
   `EVAL_TUNE_DATA_ROOT` env override, or a `--tune-root <dir>` flag), so a
   test can point `--tune` at a temp directory holding a copy of
   `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` without touching the repo file.
2. The `--watchdog` cases in `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` run the
   real CLI against that per-test temp root; the CSV digest check and
   `journalsOwnedBy(run.pid)` assertions scan the temp root only — no read or
   write of `REPO_ROOT/src/data` remains in those cases.
3. Two concurrent full-suite `npm test` runs leave `evaluate-tune-progress`
   green (the shared-`src/data` race is eliminated structurally, not
   probabilistically).
4. Every other `evaluate-tune-progress` assertion still holds: per-run
   progress lines, no `[tune]` leak into stdout, four artifacts written, and
   the off-by-default and bad-budget (exit 2) cases.
5. The seam cannot silently diverge from the sweep's config reads: a
   redirected data root combined with a **value-changing** `--set` emits a
   stderr warning that the edit targets the redirected root while the sweep
   reads the bundled config store, and the seam is documented in the CLI
   `--help`/docs as a test-isolation hook.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A developer running `npm test` in parallel no longer sees a spurious
`evaluate-tune-progress` watchdog failure caused by another suite's
transient `src/data/*.tune-journal`.

## Constraints

- **Behaviour parity (gym↔game):** this is a test-isolation change to the
  `--tune` verification harness, not gameplay; no production game behaviour
  changes.
- **No silent divergence:** the candidate sweep's config reads go through the
  bundled config store (`src/data/*.csv` via Vite `?raw`, e.g.
  `src/core/bundledConfig.ts`), so a data-root override that only redirects
  the edit/journal target must be a documented test-isolation seam with a
  warning on value-changing edits — not a path for real tuning runs to point
  at a different CSV.
- Existing tests only ever issue **byte-level no-op edits** (`boss.health=1`),
  so redirecting the edit target is behaviour-identical for the suite; the
  seam must keep that true.
- Keep the change minimal: only `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` and
  the CLI seam; do **not** refactor `evaluate-failfast.test.ts` or
  `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` (producer decision, Q2) and do not
  entangle the product-level concurrency work in AH-0MW25VH540078FDK.
- Work must happen in the worktree created by `implement.py start` (never the
  main checkout) per project rules.

## Existing state

- `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`: `CSV` is hard-coded to
  `resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'src/data/enemy-configs.csv')`; `csvDigest()` reads the
  real file; `journalsOwnedBy(pid)` does `readdirSync(join(REPO_ROOT,
  'src/data'))` and counts any journal whose recorded pid matches the spawned
  CLI, plus any unparseable journal (`catch { return true }`).
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (line ~428) hard-codes
  `resolvePath(import.meta.dirname, '..')` + `src/data` + `tuneFile`; there is
  no override today. `executeTune()` (line ~657) resolves the CSV, journals it
  before editing, and the `main()` reconcile (line ~804) restores stale
  journals for the resolved path.
- The observed flake predates the pid-scope fix; commit `88e6827a`
  (AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS) already scoped the journal assertion to the run's own
  pid, which is why reruns were green and the remaining gap is the letter of
  AC1 plus the two tight residual windows.

## Desired change

1. Add the data-root override to `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (env var preferred:
   zero public CLI surface, trivially injected via `cliSpawnEnv()` in
   `scripts/cliChildEnv.ts`; a `--tune-root <dir>` flag is the acceptable
   alternative and then needs `--help` + `evaluate.d.mts` + `docs/` sync).
2. In `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`: create a per-test temp data
   root (`mkdtempSync`), copy the shipped `enemy-configs.csv` into it, spawn
   with the override, and point `csvDigest()` and `journalsOwnedBy()` at the
   temp root (parameterise the dir instead of `REPO_ROOT/src/data`).
3. Emit the stderr warning in `executeTune()` when an override is combined
   with an edit whose `changed` is true; document the seam.

## Key Files

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — add the data-root override to
  `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (and the stderr warning near `attempt` in
  `executeTune()`).
- `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` — per-test temp data root; digest
  and journal assertions scoped to it; update the file-header comment.
- `scripts/cliChildEnv.ts` — inject the override env var per spawn.
- `scripts/evaluate.d.mts` — type the new option if a `--tune-root` flag is
  chosen.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` (crash-safe journal §) / `docs/EVALUATION.md` — document
  the test-isolation seam.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` / `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — referenced only
  to confirm the sweep read path (no change).

## Related work

- **AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS** (completed, `88e6827a`) — the pid-scoped
  `journalsOwnedBy` fix this item builds on; partial overlap, antecedent.
- **AH-0MVSE1OPF008G1SB** (completed) — per-run progress + `--watchdog`
  (parent of this test file).
- **AH-0MVSE1A7O002PXAO** (completed) — crash-safe tune CSV journal.
- **AH-0MW25VH540078FDK** (open) — serialise concurrent `--tune` runs on the
  same balance CSV (shared journal path); product-level, related, out of
  scope here.
- **AH-0MW0Q1DCZ006AUGP** (completed) — weapon catalogue CSV codec (the
  item that discovered this flake, `discovered-from:`).
- **AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7** (completed, epic) — data-driven weapon tuning.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the override is used only by tests, and existing test runs
  keep every edit a byte-level no-op, so no real tuning run is affected.
- **Risk:** a future test/run combines the override with a value-changing
  edit and silently tunes nothing → mitigated by the AC5 stderr warning and
  docs.
- **Risk (scope creep):** threading the override into the config store's
  `?raw` loads would make real edits honour the temp root but is far larger
  and touches production load paths — explicitly out of scope; the warning +
  docs approach is proportionate for a test-isolation seam.
- **Risk:** the CLI parses options from argv only today; an env override
  must be documented in the source and the file-header comment so future
  readers understand why the test no longer reads the repo dir.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (2026-11-13, asked by Map): "Scope: the pid-scope fix already closed the
  recorded flake; how should this item proceed? A) per-test temp data root
  (CLI seam) — recommended; B) close as already addressed; C) minimal
  hardening." — Answer (producer): **A**. Source: interactive reply on
  work item AH-0MW22FTXP004Z4G5 (comment AH-C0MWF28EGI0074O58). Research:
  verified `resolveTuneCsvPath()` hard-codes the repo data root and the
  config store reads CSVs via `?raw` imports, so a seam is required for A.
- Q2 (2026-11-13, asked by Map): "If A, also refactor
  `evaluate-failfast.test.ts` to a temp root, or only
  `evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`?" — Answer (producer): **only
  `evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`** (as recommended). Source: interactive
  reply. Constraint recorded above; failfast's edit discipline already holds
  and widening scope risks entangling AH-0MW25VH540078FDK.

---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS** – [test-failure] scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts > --watchdog bounded-runtime guard (AC2/AC6) > aborts with exit 124, names the phase and restores the CSV — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MVSE1PG7006XBZ9** – Docs, help sync and verification evidence re-run (completed)
- **AH-0MVSE1OPF008G1SB** – Per-run progress output and opt-in sweep watchdog (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac2, acceptance, assertion, asserts, bounded (+69 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac2, ac6, acceptance, assertion, asserts (+69 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: ac2, acceptance, asserts, bounded, cannot (+62 more)

---

- 2026-11-13T14:47Z — Plan completed (auto-skip). Pre-check returned Extra Small / Low risk → decision: skip. Six automated review stages all passed. AC coverage: proceed (100%). No children created; item ready for direct implementation.

## Problem statement

The ring-timing CLI's operator-facing text report mixes per-seed and multi-seed
figures. `formatRingTimingReport` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) renders:

- means over the seed set for `deployments`, `measured runs`, `total`, `banked salvage` and `ring secured`;
- but **seed 1's own value** for `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` (`report.runs[0]?.retryMinutes`, `runs[0]?.betweenSortieMinutes`, `runs[0]?.retakeMinutes` / `runs[0]?.expectedRetakes`).

With the default three-seed evidence set the two halves of one report therefore
describe different populations.

## Evidence

`npm run ring-timing` (2026-11-11, worktree of AH-0MW9VATHR0003WTJ, exit 0):

```text
Ring 2 · grind · seeds 1, 2, 3
  retries            55.0 min
  total              116.4 min (min 112.7, max 123.4)
```

The committed artefact (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, revision
`e873e8c3`) records per-seed `retryMinutes` of **55 / 50 / 55** — a mean of
**53.3**, not 55.0. `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline* consequently
quotes "55 of its 116.4 min (≈47 %)", pairing seed 1's retry total with the
mean total (the mean-based share is ≈45.8 %). `between sorties` and
`exposed re-capture` happen to be seed-invariant today, so only the retry line
is visibly wrong — but the rendering is one bug, not one line.

## Expected behaviour

Every metric line in the text report describes the same population (the seed
set), consistent with the JSON artefact: mean plus min–max for the per-run
totals, or an explicitly labelled seed-1 sample. The report-rendering test
(`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` § *report rendering*) should pin a
multi-seed case where the seeds differ, so the mixing cannot return.

## Acceptance criteria

- `formatRingTimingReport` renders `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` from the multi-seed aggregate (mean, with min–max where the JSON summary carries it), or labels them as a single seed; no line silently reports seed 1 as the seed-set figure.
- A report-rendering test feeds a multi-seed report whose per-seed retry totals differ and asserts the rendered value is the mean, not seed 1's.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline* quotes the retry minutes and share from the aggregate consistent with the rendered report and the committed artefact.
- Full project test suite passes.

## Notes

- Found by the verification slice `Record the ring 2 before/after split and verify the acceptance criteria (AH-0MW9VATHR0003WTJ)`; deliberately not fixed there (that item's scope forbids code changes).
- No behaviour or measured value changes: this is a reporting/consistency fix only.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5** – Rebalance ring 2's grind budget: measured 48.1 min vs the authored 90–120 min window (open)
- **AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X** – Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured 16.4 min vs the authored 40–60 min window (open)
- **AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL** – Restore ring 2's 70–100 window and regenerate the ring-timing evidence (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: acceptance, aggregate, asserts, banked, based (+119 more)
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, aggregate, asserts, banked, based (+109 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: acceptance, aggregate, artefact, asserts, based (+104 more)
## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-14)

Four children, test-first dependency order (3 planned + 1 auto-closed coverage gap):

1. **Test: report rendering pins multi-seed retry aggregates (AH-0MWGVXB95002W7KI)** — task, low. Pins parent AC 2: a multi-seed report whose per-seed retry totals differ must render the aggregate mean, never seed 1's; also pins the between-sorties and exposed-re-capture lines.
2. **Implement: render retry/between-sortie/recapture from the seed aggregate (AH-0MWGVXJ5V008QV50)** — bug, low. Adds `betweenSortieMinutes` / `retryMinutes` / `retakeMinutes` / `expectedRetakes` `RingTimingStats` to `RingTimingSummary`, renders the three report lines from the aggregates in `formatRingTimingReport`, and regenerates the committed baseline artefact (deterministic; additive summary fields). Depends on 1.
3. **Docs: EVALUATION.md retry share from the aggregate (AH-0MWGVXRFS009HBR5)** — docs, low. Quotes the retry minutes + share from the aggregate in `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline*, consistent with the rendered report and the committed artefact. Depends on 2.
4. **Close coverage gap: Full project test suite passes. (AH-0MWGW08C0006CDUX)** — task, medium, auto-created by the AC coverage review; verifies the full suite via the test skill at the dev-push gate.

Vertical slicing: each phase is a thin end-to-end slice (test → code + evidence → docs); the scope is Small, so no further phasing is needed.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-15: plan re-run (idempotent, post-implement-drive stop) — plan already complete: 4 children in test-first dependency order with edges wired (test -> implement -> docs -> coverage-gap); coverage review re-verified (proceed, 100%, triage items excluded); parent restored to `plan_complete`; no new children or plan blocks created.
- 2026-11-14: initial decomposition — 3 children created (test-first), dependency edges wired (implement → test; docs → implement); AC coverage review auto-closed the suite-gate gap (created AH-0MWGW08C0006CDUX) and advanced the parent to `plan_complete`; parent estimate refreshed via the effort-and-risk skill (Small / Medium, see its comment).

- A4 (2026-11-15 revision): plan re-run — no operator questions were asked; existing plan from 2026-11-14 treated as sufficient (Process Step 1). Final: plan unchanged, stage restored to `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No operator questions were asked in this session — a downtime-dispatched run (herdr-downtime) with no interactive approver. The plan proceeds on the documented assumptions below; all are recorded for audit.

- A1 (fix shape): extend `RingTimingSummary` with the four aggregate stats and render from them — parent AC 1's primary option ("mean, with min–max where the JSON summary carries it") — rather than re-labelling the lines as a single seed. Rationale: every other report line is already aggregate and the JSON artefact is the stated consistency reference. Final: aggregate extension.
- A2 (artefact): regenerate `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` so its JSON summary carries the new fields. Deterministic per the existing determinism test; existing mean/min/max totals must be unchanged. Final: regenerate.
- A3 (doc quote): quote the grind line's aggregate retry minutes + share in § *Measured baseline* (mirrors the old "55 of its 116.4 min" quote; the rush line's re-capture is already covered by its own reading bullet). Final: grind-line aggregate quote.
- No OPEN QUESTION entries: no producer ruling is required to proceed with this plan.

# Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured 16.4 min against the authored 40–60 min window

Discovered-from: AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V (Budget verdicts and linked rebalancing
items), part of the re-measurement chain under AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A (Re-measure
ring timing for one-level hex deployments). **Producer ruling required** — this
item records the evidence and the options; it does not decide which way the
budget should move.

## Why this item exists

`RING_TIMING_TARGETS` authors ring 1's grind window as **40–60 minutes** with a
±10 % tolerance of the window's width (**±2 minutes**), judged on the **grind**
line. The regenerated artifact (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, produced
by `AH-0MWCQ4GTE005YG02` from the shipped code) measures the shipped one-level
five-wave sortie at **16.4 minutes**, so the authored window no longer holds.
The parent's acceptance criteria forbid silently re-wording a missed budget,
so the miss is recorded here and the ruling is left to the producer.

## Measurement (source: `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, ring 1, `grind`, seeds 1–3)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verdict | **missed** (`withinWindow: false`, `withinTolerance: false`) |
| Measured total mean | **16.4256 min** (seeds: 15.7239 / 16.6383 / 16.9144) |
| Measured total min–max | **15.7239 – 16.9144 min** |
| Authored window | **40 – 60 min** |
| Tolerance | ±10 % of window width = **±2 min** (tolerance floor 38 min) |
| Delta to window floor | **−23.5744 min** below 40 min; **−21.5744 min** below the 38 min tolerance floor |
| Deployment minutes (measured, mean) | 2.2128 (1.8619 / 2.3192 / 2.4572) |
| Between-sortie minutes (modelled) | 12.0 (2 min × 6 hexes) |
| Retry minutes (measured replay) | 2.2128 (= the replayed deployment's measured length) |
| Re-capture minutes (modelled) | 0.0 (the grind line secures the ring) |
| Split check | 2.2128 + 12.0 + 2.2128 + 0.0 = 16.4256 = the total mean |
| Captured / lost sorties | 0.0 / **6.0** per run — every sortie is a first-attempt loss to enemy fire and is retried |
| Ring secured | 3 / 3 runs (the grind plays every hex, so the ring still ends secured) |
| Salvage | 0.0 banked, 15.0 forfeited (mean: 25 / 4 / 16) |

## Before/after attributable to the one-level model

| Ring 1 grind | Before (campaign slice) | After (one-level sortie) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total mean (min–max) | 54.3 (51.0–56.6) | **16.4 (15.7–16.9)** | −37.9 min |
| Verdict | in-window (40–60) | **missed (40–60)** | window no longer holds |
| Deployment minutes | 19.0 | 2.2 | −16.8 (the slice no longer climbs campaign levels past the hex's own) |
| Retry minutes | 23.3 | 2.2 | −21.1 (retry now charges the replayed deployment's measured length, not a flat 5 min) |
| Between-sortie minutes | 12.0 | 12.0 | unchanged (2 min × 6 hexes) |
| Re-capture minutes | 0.0 | 0.0 | unchanged on the grind line |
| Captured / lost | 1.3 / 4.7 | 0.0 / 6.0 | no sortie clears under the per-level arena's fire-on fidelity |
| Salvage banked / forfeited | 24.0 / 54.0 | 0.0 / 15.0 | no capture ⇒ no banking |

The dominant driver is the deployment model itself: a deployment's measured
arena time fell from ≈3.2 min to ≈0.4 min, and the retry term follows it
mechanically (retry = the replayed deployment's measured length). The
between-sortie allowance (2 min) and the re-capture allowance are unchanged and
do not drive the delta.

## Options (for the producer; not a recommendation)

1. **Re-author the ring-1 window** (e.g. from 40–60 min to a window the shipped
   one-level model measures). Cheapest, but it changes the design of record
   (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Session shape) rather than the game.
2. **Tune the authored ring data** — more hexes in ring 1, or higher
   aggression/level per hex — so a ring-1 clear takes the authored time. This
   changes gameplay pace, not the timing model.
3. **Revisit the allowances** — the between-sortie 2 minutes, the retry rule
   (one modelled replay per loss) and the rush re-capture charge. A larger
   between-sortie or retry allowance would lengthen the measured total, but it
   prices a deployment time the harness does not measure.
4. **Revisit the measurement boundary** — the per-level arena ignores the wave
   `shootEnabled` gate, so every sortie is lost to enemy fire and none is
   captured. Honouring the gate (or modelling the mini-boss encounter, also
   unmodelled) would raise captures and change the measured total; that is a
   harness/model decision (`AH-0MWCQ4FWN009J9DM` chain), not a budget re-word.

## Acceptance criteria

- The producer rules on one of the options (or another) and records the
  decision on this item; **no option is taken implicitly** by a later code or
  docs change.
- If the ruling re-authors the window, `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`, the docs guards
  (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`, `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`) and
  the quoted documents are updated together and the artifact re-judged.
- If the ruling tunes the ring data or the allowances, the artifact is
  regenerated with the documented command and the before/after evidence is
  recorded here.
- Whatever the ruling, ring 1's grind verdict is stated honestly (measured
  figure, window, delta) — never re-worded as passing.
- The full project test suite passes with the change.

**Related:** `related-to:AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A`,
`discovered-from:AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V`,
`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`
(`RING_TIMING_TARGETS`), `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Session shape.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5** – Rebalance ring 2's grind budget: measured 48.1 min vs the authored 90–120 min window (open)
- **AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL** – Restore ring 2's 70–100 window and regenerate the ring-timing evidence (completed)
- **AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V** – Budget verdicts and linked rebalancing items (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mwcowsvn003x81a, acceptance, aggression, allowance, allowances (+192 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mwcowsvn003x81a, 0mwcq4htc004u73v, acceptance, aggression, also (+171 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: 0mwcowsvn003x81a, 0mwcq4fwn009j9dm, acceptance, aggression, allowance (+168 more)

| Total mean (min–max) | 116.4 (112.7–123.4) | **48.1 (42.4–58.4)** | −68.3 min |
| Verdict | in-window (90–120) | **missed (90–120)** | window no longer holds |
| Deployment minutes | 39.1 | 12.1 | −27.0 (the slice no longer climbs campaign levels past the hex's own) |
| Retry minutes | 53.3 | 12.1 | −41.2 (retry now charges the replayed deployment's measured length, not a flat 5 min) |
| Between-sortie minutes | 24.0 | 24.0 | unchanged (2 min × 12 hexes) |
| Re-capture minutes | 0.0 | 0.0 | unchanged on the grind line |
| Captured / lost | 1.3 / 10.7 | 0.0 / 12.0 | no sortie clears under the per-level arena's fire-on fidelity |
| Salvage banked / forfeited | 22.3 / 173.3 | 0.0 / 84.7 | no capture ⇒ no banking |

The dominant driver is the deployment model itself: a deployment's measured
arena time fell from ≈3.2 min to ≈1.0 min on ring 2's hexes, and the retry term
follows it mechanically (retry = the replayed deployment's measured length).
The between-sortie allowance (2 min) and the re-capture allowance are unchanged
and do not drive the delta. Note that ring 2's twelve 2-minute visits now
account for half the measured total — the largest remaining modelled term.

## Options (for the producer; not a recommendation)

1. **Re-author the ring-2 window** (e.g. from 90–120 min to a window the shipped
   one-level model measures). Cheapest, but it changes the design of record
   (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Session shape) rather than the game.
2. **Tune the authored ring data** — more hexes in ring 2, or higher
   aggression/level per hex — so a ring-2 clear takes the authored time. This
   changes gameplay pace, not the timing model.
3. **Revisit the allowances** — the between-sortie 2 minutes (24.0 of the
   48.1 measured minutes here), the retry rule (one modelled replay per loss)
   and the rush re-capture charge. A larger between-sortie or retry allowance
   would lengthen the measured total, but it prices time the harness does not
   measure.
4. **Revisit the measurement boundary** — the per-level arena ignores the wave
   `shootEnabled` gate, so every sortie is lost to enemy fire and none is
   captured. Honouring the gate (or modelling the mini-boss encounter, also
   unmodelled) would raise captures and change the measured total; that is a
   harness/model decision (`AH-0MWCQ4FWN009J9DM` chain), not a budget re-word.

## Acceptance criteria

- The producer rules on one of the options (or another) and records the
  decision on this item; **no option is taken implicitly** by a later code or
  docs change.
- If the ruling re-authors the window, `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`, the docs guards
  (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`, `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`) and
  the quoted documents are updated together and the artifact re-judged.
- If the ruling tunes the ring data or the allowances, the artifact is
  regenerated with the documented command and the before/after evidence is
  recorded here.
- Whatever the ruling, ring 2's grind verdict is stated honestly (measured
  figure, window, delta) — never re-worded as passing.
- The full project test suite passes with the change.

**Related:** `related-to:AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A`,
`discovered-from:AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V`,
`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`
(`RING_TIMING_TARGETS`), `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Session shape.
data.title: Rebalance ring 2's grind budget: measured 48.1 min vs the authored 90–120 min window

Parent: AH-0MWCB6021008L4YN (Ring-timing text report prints seed 1's retry, between-sortie and re-capture minutes as if they were the multi-seed figures).

## Goal (user story)

As a ring-timing harness maintainer, I want the operator-facing text report's metric lines to describe the same population (the seed set), so the report-rendering test pins that a multi-seed report whose seeds differ renders the aggregate, never seed 1's sample.

## Summary

Extend `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` § *report rendering* with a multi-seed case whose per-seed retry totals differ, asserting the rendered `retries` (and `between sorties` / `exposed re-capture`) lines show the aggregate mean — red against the current `formatRingTimingReport`, green after the implement sibling lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A report-rendering test feeds a multi-seed report (seeds 1-3) whose per-seed retry totals differ (a seed-varying fake deployment runner) and asserts the rendered `retries` line equals the mean of the per-run `retryMinutes`, not seed 1's value.
- The same test (or a sibling in the same describe block) asserts the `between sorties` and `exposed re-capture` lines render aggregate figures (mean, with min-max where the JSON summary carries them), never `report.runs[0]` values.
- The single-seed case keeps working: with `seeds: [1]` the header reads `seed 1` and the lines render that seed's sole figures.
- The new test is observed failing against the current `formatRingTimingReport` (red first) and passes once the implement sibling lands; no existing test's assertions are weakened.

## Minimal implementation

- Add a seed-varying fake runner (e.g. parameterise the existing `fakeRunner` helper by `request.seed`, or add a seed-specific runner) so `retryMinutes` differs across seeds 1-3.
- Build `simulateRingTiming({ ringIndex: 1, strategy: 'grind', seeds: [1, 2, 3], hexes: modelRing(), runDeployment: <seed-varying runner> })` and assert the rendered lines show the means; add a rush case for the `exposed re-capture` line.
- Run the changed-scope test gate through the test skill (`/skill:test`, never ad-hoc test commands) to confirm red-then-green.

## Constraints

- Test-only item: no production-code changes here (the fix lands in the sibling implement item).
- Deterministic and fast: model ring + fake runners only, never the real arena or the wall clock.
- UK English throughout.

## Risky assumptions

- A seed-varying fake runner is the cleanest way to make per-seed retry totals differ without the real arena. Success threshold: the test is red on today's `formatRingTimingReport`, proving it pins the population-mixing regression.

## Impact

The ring-timing report-rendering suite now pins that a multi-seed report renders the seed-set aggregate — never seed 1's sample — so the retry/between-sortie/re-capture population-mixing regression is caught by CI before it can reach operators.

# Author shipped hex variety content on ring 2 (personalities, contracts, landmarks)

## Problem statement

As a player pushing into later rings, I want the **shipped** rings to actually
author hex variety, so the shipped machinery delivers the variety it was built
for instead of living only in the ring-3 verification sample. Today the shipped
table (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` + `hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv`)
authors **no** variety, so no shipped hex offers a personality, a contract or a
landmark.

## Users (with example user stories)

- **The returning ring-2 player** — "I've captured hexes in every prong of ring
  1; I want at least one ring-2 hex to fight differently, one to offer a
  worthwhile optional objective, and one set-piece that asks for a real
  decision, otherwise the ring is the same chores at an angrier number."
- **The strategist** — "I want to read each hex's personality, contract and
  landmark in the map's known-ahead intel before I commit a life, so the
  variety informs my choice instead of gambling it."

## Acceptance Criteria

- `hex-r2-1` (the-siege-leviathan) authors the `nebula` personality, `hex-r2-6`
  (cobalt-siege) authors a contract (objective "Break the siege line then hold
  the hex", bonus +100 salvage / +1 core), and `hex-r2-7` (the-static-prophet)
  authors the `fortress` landmark — all in `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`,
  mirrored byte-for-value in `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv` (CSV-seed parity test
  green). Ring 1 stays the plain tutorial ring (no variety authored).
- `validateRingDefinitions(2, HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS)` stays green, and a
  shipped-data test asserts `buildHexMapModel` publishes the authored
  personality (id + projectile-drag mechanic), the contract (objective, bonus,
  `open` status) and the landmark (type + fortress progress `0/2`) before
  commitment.
- Ring 2's authored `baseAggression` values are unchanged (`2, 2, 5, 2, 5, 2, 2,
  5, 6, 2, 5, 8`); the three variety hexes stay at the aggression-2 survivable
  floor and their personalities/landmarks add no aggression step; `hex-r2-12`
  remains the ring's strict weapon/aggression maximum.
- The `nebula` personality is genuinely felt: it sits on a weapon-granting hex
  (`hex-r2-1` grants `arc`), so the boss's demonstrated volley is slowed by the
  shared drag factor (no new code path).
- The ring-timing evaluation is re-run and recorded; the ring-2 measurement and
  the authored aggression band are unchanged (variety data does not feed the
  harness).
- GDD §8.2 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` name the shipped variety hexes
  and what each authors.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players will finally meet the variety the Hangar War was built for on the ring
they actually grind: `hex-r2-1` fights differently (a drifting slow `arc`
volley), `hex-r2-6` offers an optional contract for extra banked salvage, and
`hex-r2-7` is a fortress capture that needs two passes.

## Constraints

- **Data change only.** Extend `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` and mirror it in
  `hex-ring-2.csv`. The vocabulary, loud validation, known-ahead intel,
  resolvers, persistence and docs already ship — no new code path is expected.
- **Existing economy.** Contract and cache rewards use the shipped currencies
  through `bankSalvage`; no new currency and no special-mission-style reward
  (those stay with AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55). The +100/+1 contract bonus sits below
  the 140-salvage cache payout.
- **Survivable band.** The three variety hexes are aggression-2 survivors; no
  `berserker` personality (it adds an aggression step) may be placed on one.
- **Mechanic visibility.** `nebula` only tunes the boss's demonstrated volley,
  so it must sit on a weapon-granting hex — it does (`hex-r2-1` grants `arc`).
- **One weapon hex.** `hex-r2-12` (`nova`) stays the single, strict hardest
  weapon hex; a `cache` can never be the weapon hex (already validated).
- **Leave the special mission alone.** `hex-r2-3` already authors the
  `isSpecialMission` + `hull-3` reward; do not stack a landmark/contract on it.
- **Gym↔game parity.** No scene change expected; if any is needed it must land
  in the shared core, never a per-scene copy.
- **CSV safety.** The contract objective contains no comma, so the seed stays
  unquoted and parseable.

## Existing state

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` authors rings 1 (6) and 2 (12) only, with no
  `personality`/`contract`/`landmark` on any row; `hex-ring-1.csv` and
  `hex-ring-2.csv` mirror it with empty variety columns.
- `VARIETY_RING_DEFINITIONS` in `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`
  is the authored **ring-3 sample** showing the intended shape (five
  personalities incl. both bounded mechanics, two contracts, one fortress, one
  cache) — fixture data, not shipped content.
- `validateRingDefinitions` already rejects unknown ids, malformed contracts,
  cache-on-weapon-hex and duplicate set-pieces; `buildHexMapModel` /
  `buildHexIntel` already publish personality/contract/landmark intel.
- Ring 2 aggressions `2,2,5,2,5,2,2,5,6,2,5,8` are pinned by
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` (AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC band). The
  ring-timing baseline (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`,
  `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`) does not model variety, so authoring it does
  not move the measured number.
- `hex-r2-3` is ring 2's authored special mission (`hull-3`).

## Desired change

Author variety on three distinct ring-2 hexes, all at the aggression-2
survivable floor (producer-confirmed 2026-11-15, Q1 = a, Q2 = a, Q3 = a):

| Hex | Aggression | Authored axis | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hex-r2-1` (the-siege-leviathan) | 2 | `personality` | `nebula` — shared projectile-drag mechanic; the hex grants `arc`, so its demonstrated volley drifts slow (≈61 % speed, `NEBULA_PROJECTILE_DRAG 1.65`) |
| `hex-r2-6` (cobalt-siege) | 2 | `contract` | objective "Break the siege line then hold the hex"; +100 salvage, +1 core, banked on capture via `bankSalvage` |
| `hex-r2-7` (the-static-prophet) | 2 | `landmark` | `fortress` — two capture passes (`FORTRESS_CAPTURE_PASSES = 2`), keeps its `extra-life` grant |

Ring 1 stays plain. No `baseAggression`, grant, boss or weaknesses change on any
row; only the three variety fields are added.

## Key Files

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — add the variety fields to three ring-2 rows.
- `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv` — mirror the same values in the seed columns.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` — add shipped-data assertions that the
  authored variety is present and published.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — validation only; no code change expected.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — no change expected; read model already
  publishes the axes.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§8.2 *Hex variety*) — name the shipped
  variety hexes.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — record which shipped hexes author variety.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` + `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — re-measure and
  record (expected unchanged).

## Related work

- discovered-from: AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG (hex variety epic — machinery shipped and
  verified against the ring-3 sample).
- AH-0MWEW4ANW009GGX7 — data vocabulary, fixtures and loud validation.
- AH-0MWEW50B10089D4W — personality axis (config-tunes + two shared mechanics).
- AH-0MWEW58WD003NFXS — contract axis.
- AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH — ring landmarks axis.
- AH-0MWEW73WS003QFV7 — epic end-to-end verification.
- AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC — ring 2 survivable aggression band.
- AH-0MWF0CTQB001XFE1 — the authored ring-2 special mission (`hex-r2-3`).
- AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55 — special missions (special rewards stay there).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Balance risk** — the personality/fortress could lengthen the three survivor
  hexes. Mitigation: all three sit at the aggression-2 floor, `nebula` slows the
  boss volley (player-friendly), no reward is removed (`fortress` keeps
  `extra-life`), and the contract bonus is modest (+100/+1).
- **Visibility risk** — a demonstrated-volley-only personality on an
  upgrade-granting hex would be invisible; `hex-r2-1` grants `arc`, so the
  mechanic is felt.
- **Scope-creep risk** — richer variety (more hexes, ring 1 variety, a `cache`,
  new mechanics) is out of scope for the minimum; record it as linked follow-up
  work, not additions here.
- **Assumption** — the ring-timing measurement is unaffected because the harness
  does not consume variety fields; verified by re-running and recording.
- **Assumption** — `hex-r2-1`/`hex-r2-6`/`hex-r2-7` are the confirmed hexes; the
  producer approved them as the recommendation's concrete examples.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- Q: "Q1 — Content scope: one personality + one contract + one landmark on
  ring-2 hexes, ring 1 plain? (a) suggested minimum, (b) richer spread, (c) exact
  table" — Answer (producer, 2026-11-15): **(a) suggested minimum** — one of each
  on three distinct ring-2 hexes, ring 1 plain. Source: interactive reply on
  AH-0MWH4F375000X08G comment AH-C0MWHC11BN001YSIH.
- Q: "Q2 — Personality choice: (a) `nebula` shared mechanic on a weapon-granting
  survivor, (b) config-tune, (c) `berserker`, (d) implementer picks" — Answer
  (producer, 2026-11-15): **(a) `nebula`** on `hex-r2-1` (grants `arc`,
  aggression 2). Source: interactive reply, same comment.
- Q: "Q3 — Landmark choice: (a) `fortress` keeping the hex's grant, (b) `cache`
  payout, (c) either" — Answer (producer, 2026-11-15): **(a) `fortress`** on
  `hex-r2-7` (keeps `extra-life`). Source: interactive reply, same comment.

Research summary: the intended shape was read from the item's own "Suggested
minimum shape (producer to confirm)" plus the ring-3 fixture sample
(`VARIETY_RING_DEFINITIONS`); ring-2 aggressions are pinned by
`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` (AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC); `hexBoss.ts` shows
`nebula` tunes only the demonstrated volley, hence the weapon-granting-hex
constraint; the ring-timing harness (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) does not read
variety fields, so the measured baseline is expected to be unchanged.
data.title: Author shipped hex variety content on ring 2 (personalities, contracts, landmarks)

# Hangar owned-row upgrade affordance

The hangar screen's owned rows for level-bearing weapons/power-ups show the current level and an upgrade action with its price, disabled visibly when unaffordable or capped; all non-upgradeable rows are byte-identical to today.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An owned row for a level-bearing weapon/power-up shows its current permanent level and an upgrade action with the two-currency price (e.g. `UPGRADE · 25 min`), rendered through the shared `renderHangarScreen`/`buildHangarScreenModel` path (no per-scene copy).
2. The upgrade button is visibly disabled when the player cannot afford it or the kind is at the max-permanent-level ceiling; activating it persists through the hangar-war store via the pure economy rule — no purchase logic in scene code.
